final_answer:
antibiotic resistance occurs when bacteria evolve mechanisms to survive exposure to antibiotics. this is driven by natural selection: when antibiotics are used, they kill susceptible bacteria, but any bacteria with genetic mutations that confer resistance survive. these resistant bacteria then reproduce, passing on their resistance traits to offspring. over time, this leads to a population of bacteria that is resistant to the antibiotic.

overprescription of antibiotics accelerates this process. when antibiotics are used unnecessarily or inappropriately (e.g., for viral infections), they expose large numbers of bacteria to the drug. this increases the chances that resistant strains will emerge and spread. additionally, incomplete courses of antibiotics allow some bacteria to survive, giving them more opportunities to develop resistance. by reducing the effectiveness of antibiotics, overprescription makes infections harder to treat and increases the risk of untreatable diseases.
